name: Knockin Rhythm
memo: Guns N' Roses - Knockin' On Heaven's Door: rhythm. Clean-ish chorus-washed arpeggios in the verses, edge of breakup for the big choruses.

band.style_feel: slow ballad, half-time backbeat, snare on 3, soft ride/hi-hat, bass on the root; builds to a full band in the choruses
band.key: Gb major sounding (recorded a half step down; G major shapes G D Am7 / G D C in standard tuning)
parts: Part A: intro and verse - soft drums, sparse bass
Part B: chorus - fuller band, snare on the backbeat
Part C: second verse and chorus - steady, a little louder
Part D: guitar solo - full band, big sustain
Part E: long outro chorus - full band, loud and open
band.tips: Sources disagree on tempo (about 66 BPM with a variable feel; automatic detectors report 89 or 133, which are double/triple readings), so set the Trio+ by ear and tap the tempo. Play the intro chords cleanly for 2 bars before the Trio+ starts learning.

whammy.tuning: Eb standard (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb), half step down
how: Tune your guitar to standard (E A D G B E).
Turn the right knob to TRANSPOSE DOWN 1.
Press DROPTUNE (light on) before the song.
whammy.tips: Play the G-D-Am7 / G-D-C shapes as in standard tuning; the pedal sounds them a half step lower to match the recording. No whammy or octave effect is documented on the track. Alternatively retune to Eb and leave the pedal off.

originals.guitar: Gibson Explorer (1958) / Gibson Flying V (1959 Korina), reported for the solo

guitar.position: neck pickup for the verse arpeggios, bridge pickup for the choruses; volume full, tone around 7
guitar.tone_notes: Warm humbucker tone with a chorused clean verse and a singing, sustained lead; a single-coil guitar will be thinner, so add a little gain and roll back treble on the lead patch. Sources disagree on which guitar was used for the solo.

name: Knockin Lead
memo: Guns N' Roses - Knockin' On Heaven's Door: lead. Singing, sustained Brown-amp solo tone with a touch of delay and reverb.
